historical_references.reference: In the 16th century, a French monk named Jean des Mares, also known as Jean de Marcellis, claimed to have had a vision in which an angel revealed to him the true name of God as Elionor or Elyonel. This name, according to des Mares, was a combination of the Hebrew words 'El' (God) and 'Yonah' (dove), symbolizing the descending Holy Spirit.

In the early 20th century, a spiritualist named Rosicrucian Max Heindel claimed that the name Elyon or Elyonel was an ancient name for God, derived from the Hebrew word 'El' (God) and the Aramaic word 'Elyon' (most high). Heindel believed that this name represented God as the Supreme Ruler of the Universe.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Elyonel' has seen modern usage primarily in the context of role-playing games (RPGs), fantasy literature, anime and manga. In tabletop RPGs, Elyonel may be used as the name of a powerful deity or an important NPC. In web novels, it might be the name of a character in an epic fantasy story. In anime and manga, Elyonel could be the name of a heroic character in a fantasy series or a villainous one in a dark fantasy story. Elyonel's usage in these modern contexts reflects the general trend towards the revival and expansion of fantasy and mythology in various forms of media.
